messages:
aisha: Heads-up — we're seeing a sudden p99 token latency spike for hosted inference in eastus (cluster eastus-gpu-1). Started ~02:05 UTC, p99 jumping from ~120ms to ~420ms and some 5-15% tail packet loss on east-west host links. :eyes:
kevin: Which hosts? any recent infra config pushes?
aisha: Initial blast radius looks like nodes gpu-23..gpu-49 (27 hosts). I pulled tcpdump/iperf quickly — shows packet loss and retransmits between 10.0.5.23 <-> 10.0.5.24. No obvious NIC errors in dmesg.
kevin: Can you paste tc output from one affected host? especially qdisc on bond0/eth0
aisha: here's tc and ethtool dump from gpu-23:
```
$ sudo tc qdisc show dev bond0
qdisc ingress ffff: dev bond0 parent ffff:fff1 ----------------
qdisc fq_codel 8019: parent 1: limit 10240 quantum 1514 target 5ms interval 100ms ecn
qdisc tbf 1: root refcnt 2 rate 800mbit burst 1600kb lat 50ms

$ sudo ethtool bond0
Supported ports: [ TP ]
Supported link modes:  10000baseT/Full ...
Current message level: 0x00000007 (7)
Link detected: yes
MTU: 9000
```
aisha: Note: tbf + fq_codel stacked on same dev, and we have jumbo MTU 9000.
maria: Hmm stack ordering looks suspect — fq_codel should be root for per-flow fairness, but adding tbf underneath can starve RDMA/KV traffic. Did the qos daemon push a policy?
ops-bot: config-sync: applied policy "egress-throttle-2026-03" to hostname-prefix gpu- (rollout id: r-2026-03-312)
kevin: That rollout happened at 02:00 UTC. ops-bot, link the change?
deploy-bot: Change r-2026-03-312: QoS policy update by infra-qos (patch): added fq_codel + tbf on bond0 to limit egress burst. Targets: eastus-gpu-1. Rollout: 02:00 -> 02:03 UTC.
samir: If tbf is above fq_codel or vice-versa misordered it will reclassify packets unpredictably. Also RDMA/GPUDirect can be sensitive to shaping; we saw similar symptoms when ingress policing collided with kernel offloads.
jules: Are we certain it's shaping and not a downstream switch flapping? I don't see interface errors though.
kevin: aisha, can you run `tc -s qdisc` and `cat /proc/net/dev` and a quick `perf top` to rule out CPU saturation?
aisha: tc -s qdisc shows high drop counters on fq_codel 'drops 1240' and tbf 'overlimits 870'. /proc/net/dev shows rx/tx bytes normal, no carrier errors. perf top not showing user CPU spikes.
maria: Ok that's consistent with host-level shaping causing drops. Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback QoS policy, 2) change tbf params (increase burst/lat), 3) apply per-class exemption for RDMA/kv-store ports.
samir: Can we do a targeted rollback on 3 canary hosts and re-measure p99? Prefer minimal blast radius.
kevin: +1. Abort the global rollout. Ops-bot, initiate rollback to previous QoS config on eastus-gpu-1.
ops-bot: rollback job scheduled: r-2026-03-312 -> previous (r-2026-02-214). Targeting hosts: gpu-23,gpu-24,gpu-25 for canary at 02:35 UTC.
aisha: Running quick test after removing tbf on gpu-23:
```
sudo tc qdisc del dev bond0 parent 1: handle 8000: tbf rate 800mbit burst 1600kb lat 50ms || true
uname -a; # still same kernel
iperf3 -c 10.0.5.24 -u -b 5G -t 10
# packet loss drops to <1% after tbf removed locally, p99 for inference flows down to ~140ms
```
kevin: Excellent. Rollback look good for canary?
maria: Monitor for a few minutes then unroll to remainder of affected hosts if stable. Also add a follow-up to change QoS daemon to not stack tbf under fq_codel by default, and to whitelist RDMA/GPUDirect ports.
jules: Can we also gate future rollouts with a quick latency smoke test for inference SLOs? This one slipped through because the QA run only checked bandwidth not latency.
samir: I'll open a PR with a kernel/ci smoke that runs a short tail-latency check against a small model behind the QoS change.
aisha: Current status: canary hosts rolled back, p99 recovered to ~130-160ms, packet loss negligible. Initiating rollback to all 27 hosts now.
kevin: Thanks everyone. Post-mortem checklist: root cause = qos-policy misconfiguration (tbf + fq_codel stacking + no RDMA exemptions) causing host-level egress policing to drop packets and spike inference tail latency. Action items: rollback complete, patch qos daemon, add smoke tests, and update runbook. Assign owners?
maria: I'll own runbook/update. samir owns smoke tests. kevin will coordinate QoS daemon patch and staged rollout. aisha will follow-up with detailed logs for postmortem.
aisha: filing follow-up incident ticket with logs and tc dumps. :white_check_mark:
